{{short description|Metaphor originating from goal sports}}
'''Moving the goalposts''' (or '''shifting the goalposts''') is a [[metaphor]], derived from [[Goal (sport)|goal]]-based sports such as [[football]] and [[hockey]], that means to change the rule or criterion ("goal") of a process or competition while it is still in progress, in such a way that the new goal offers one side an advantage or disadvantage.<ref name="phrases">{{cite web |url=http://www.phrases.org.uk/meanings/251400.html |title=Moving the goalposts |publisher=Phrases.org.uk |access-date=2011-12-20 |archive-date=2019-05-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190518160444/https://www.phrases.org.uk/meanings/251400.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Etymology==
{{wikt|move the goalposts|shift the goalposts}}
This phrase is British in origin and derives from sports that use [[goalposts]].<ref>{{Cite Merriam-Webster|move/shift the goalposts}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Safire |first=William |title=On Language; Moving the Goalposts |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/10/28/magazine/on-language-moving-the-goalposts.html |access-date=1 February 2017 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=28 October 1990 |archive-date=18 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190518160441/https://www.nytimes.com/1990/10/28/magazine/on-language-moving-the-goalposts.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The figurative use alludes to the perceived unfairness in changing the [[goal]] one is trying to achieve after the process one is engaged in (such as a game of [[Association football|football]]) has already started.<ref name="phrases" />

==Logical fallacy==
Moving the goalposts is an [[informal fallacy]] in which evidence presented in response to a specific claim is dismissed and some other (often greater) evidence is demanded.  That is, after an attempt has been made to score a goal, the goalposts are moved to exclude the attempt.<ref name="clark">{{cite book|last1=Clark |first1=Jef |last2=Clark |first2=Theo |title=Humbug! The Skeptic's Field Guide to Spotting Fallacies in Thinking |date=2005 |isbn=0-646-44477-8 |page=101|publisher=Theo Clark }}</ref>  The problem with changing the rules of the game is that the meaning of the result is changed, too.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hobbs |first=Jeremy |title=Moving the Goal Posts |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/11/22/opinion/moving-the-goal-posts.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=November 21, 2011 |access-date=February 19, 2013 |archive-date=June 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621070306/https://www.nytimes.com/2011/11/22/opinion/moving-the-goal-posts.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The opposite of moving the goalposts is '''lowering the bar'''.

==Use==
Some include this metaphor as a description of a tactic of [[workplace bullying]]. In such cases, re-defining another's goals may be intentionally devised so as to assure that they will never be able to finally achieve the ever-shifting goals.<ref>{{cite web |website=[[Royal College of Psychiatrists]] |url=https://www.rcpsych.ac.uk/members/workforce-wellbeing-hub/psychiatrists-support-service/helpsheets/bullying-and-harassment?searchTerms=moving%20the%20goalposts#faq-accoridon-collapse79a07248-3476-450b-b397-e112e30436fc |title=Bullying and harassment &sect; What is bullying? |access-date=14 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427073350/https://www.rcpsych.ac.uk/members/workforce-wellbeing-hub/psychiatrists-support-service/helpsheets/bullying-and-harassment#faq-accoridon-collapse79a07248-3476-450b-b397-e112e30436fc |archive-date=27 Apr 2025 |location=United Kingdom |language=en |url-status=live |quote=moving the goalposts – setting objectives which subtly change and are not achievable.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Field |first1=Tim |date=1996 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9T9mn72jffkC&dq=bullying+and+shifting+the+goal+posts&pg=PA60&q=shifting+goalposts |title=Bully in Sight: How to Predict, Resist, Challenge and Combat Workplace Bullying |page=60 |publisher=Success Unlimited |location=Great Britain |isbn=978-0-9529121-0-1 |access-date=14 June 2025 |language=en |quote=By constantly shifting the goalposts, a person can never achieve their tasks [...] |archive-date=28 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260228194326/https://books.google.com/books?pg=PA60&q=shifting+goalposts&id=9T9mn72jffkC&dq=bullying+and+shifting+the+goal+posts |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Non-metaphorical use <span class="anchor" id="In sports"></span> ==
[[File:Yasin Ehliz and David Leggio by 2eight DSC0583.jpg|thumb|Goaltender [[David Leggio]] (in goal at right) regularly moved his goalposts as a strategy to stop play until the tactic was outlawed.]]

Deliberately moving the goalposts constitutes a [[professional foul]] in [[rugby football]] and an [[unfair act]] in [[gridiron football]]. The officials are granted ''[[carte blanche]]'' to assess whatever penalty they see fit, including awarding the score for any attempt at a goal missed or invalidating any goal scored as a result of the moved goalposts. In both rugby and gridiron, goalposts are anchored into the ground; the distance they can be moved (most easily in gridiron by pulling down on one end of the crossbar to tilt both posts either to the left or the right) is far more restricted.{{Citation needed|date=July 2018}} Inadvertently moving the goalposts in a [[touchdown celebration]] is an [[unsportsmanlike conduct]] penalty of 15 yards against the offending team.

Moving goalposts is common in [[ice hockey]], where physical contact with the posts is common. If the goalposts are knocked off their moorings in the course of play, play is stopped until the goal is put back in place. If the goalposts are deliberately moved to stop an opponent from scoring, the opponent may be granted a [[penalty shot]]; if the goaltender does so, the goaltender may be ejected from the game, a rule imposed at most levels of the game in 2014 after [[David Leggio]] deliberately moved the goalposts during a two-person breakaway, believing he would have a better chance of stopping a penalty shot.<ref>Dhiren Mahiban (November 6, 2014). [http://prohockeytalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/06/report-ahl-changes-rule-following-leggio-incident/ Report: AHL changes rule following Leggio incident] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150127105338/http://prohockeytalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/06/report-ahl-changes-rule-following-leggio-incident/ |date=2015-01-27 }}. ''ProHockeyTalk.com''. Retrieved November 7, 2014.</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=2014-11-02|title=Video:AHL goalie Leggio intentionally dislodges net|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nhl/eye-on-hockey/24782337/video-ahl-goalie-david-leggio-intentionally-dislodges-net-to-stop-2-on-0|access-date=2014-11-02|work=[[CBS Sports]]|archive-date=2016-05-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160523182752/http://www.cbssports.com/nhl/eye-on-hockey/24782337/video-ahl-goalie-david-leggio-intentionally-dislodges-net-to-stop-2-on-0|url-status=live}}</ref> Leggio later used the tactic in the [[Deutsche Eishockey Liga]], where he had played since 2015; that league had not yet outlawed the maneuver,<ref>{{cite news|date=2017-12-09|title=David Leggio is up to his old tricks|work=Sporting News|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nhl/news/david-leggio-net-breakaway-video-olympics-2018-pyeongchang-del-germany/1ra12y0h7954f1u6vxlfaposd3|access-date=2017-12-10|last=Schlager|first=Brandon|archive-date=2017-12-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211053523/http://www.sportingnews.com/nhl/news/david-leggio-net-breakaway-video-olympics-2018-pyeongchang-del-germany/1ra12y0h7954f1u6vxlfaposd3|url-status=dead}}</ref> but promptly did so after Leggio's first attempt at using the tactic.<ref name="leggiorule_del">{{cite web|last1=Leahy|first1=Sarah|date=13 December 2017|title=Another league changes its rules, thanks to David Leggio|url=http://nhl.nbcsports.com/2017/12/13/another-league-changes-its-rules-thanks-to-david-leggio/|access-date=13 December 2017|website=NBC Sports|archive-date=14 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171214073555/http://nhl.nbcsports.com/2017/12/13/another-league-changes-its-rules-thanks-to-david-leggio/|url-status=live}}</ref> The DEL instead automatically [[Awarded goal|awards the goal]] to the opposing team.<ref name="leggiorule_del" /> The [[National Hockey League]] approved this rule in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gary Bettman announces new rules for next season |url=https://www.pensionplanpuppets.com/2019/6/20/18694572/nhl-gary-bettman-announces-new-rules-for-next-season-video-review-offsides-coaches-challenge |last=Hardev |date=June 20, 2019 |website=Pension Plan Puppets |access-date=September 29, 2023 |archive-date=July 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190718232707/https://www.pensionplanpuppets.com/2019/6/20/18694572/nhl-gary-bettman-announces-new-rules-for-next-season-video-review-offsides-coaches-challenge |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2009, Danish goalkeeper [[Kim Christensen (footballer, born 1979)|Kim Christensen]] was recorded on camera moving the goalposts in order to gain advantage over the opposing team. Christensen's moving the goalposts was discovered by a referee about 20 minutes into the game, but Christensen did not suffer a suspension or any fines for his actions.<ref>{{cite news|date=24 September 2009|title=Keeper guilty of moving goalposts|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/8274016.stm|access-date=1 February 2017|archive-date=23 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223034418/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/8274016.stm|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Rose|first1=Ellie|date=25 September 2009|title=Kim Christensen admits moving the goalposts|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/sep/25/kim-christensen-admits-moving-goalposts|access-date=1 February 2017|archive-date=18 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190518160440/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/sep/25/kim-christensen-admits-moving-goalposts|url-status=live}}</ref>

In May 2022, a scandal erupted when video published by ''[[Aftenposten]]'' showed [[Viking FK]]'s goalkeeper [[Patrik Gunnarsson]] reducing his goal size by moving the goalposts by {{convert|15–20|cm|sigfig=1}}, after the referee inspection but prior to kickoff, in home games during the 2022 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2022/05/31/6296828446163f45948b4616.html |title=Goalkeeper Patrik Gunnarsson accused of making his goal smaller! |date=31 May 2022 |publisher=Marca |lang=en |archive-date=1 June 2022 |access-date=1 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601144506/https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2022/05/31/6296828446163f45948b4616.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author1=Stig Nilssen |author2=Alexander Larsen |author3=Mats Haugland |title=Se video og bilder: Viking-keeperen flytter stolpene og gjør målet mindre: – Ser ikke bra ut |url=https://www.aftenposten.no/sport/i/PoQgQp/se-video-og-bilder-viking-keeperen-flytter-stolpene-og-gjoer-maalet-mindre-ser-ikke-bra-ut |date=30 May 2022 |publisher=Aftenposten |lang=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lastampa.it/sport/calcio/2022/06/01/video/scandalo_nel_calcio_norvegese_il_portiere_del_viking_fk_patrik_gunnarsson_accusato_di_truccare_la_sua_porta-5281151/ |title=Scandalo nel calcio norvegese, il portiere del Viking FK Patrik Gunnarsson accusato di 'truccare' la sua porta |date=June 2022 |publisher=La Stampa |lang=it |archive-date=2022-06-01 |access-date=2022-06-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601144505/https://www.lastampa.it/sport/calcio/2022/06/01/video/scandalo_nel_calcio_norvegese_il_portiere_del_viking_fk_patrik_gunnarsson_accusato_di_truccare_la_sua_porta-5281151/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
